message.content: {"mechanism_id":"repair_aware_resampling","target_component":"boundary_constraint_handling","observed_evidence":{"task_id":"TASK-04","trace_path":"diagnostic_trace_summary","function":"F7","seed":0,"metric":"repair_success_gap","observed_value":0.24},"causal_hypothesis":"np.clip collapses out-of-bounds coordinates onto the boundary face, producing a mutant whose displacement opposes the search direction (cosine -0.4 to -0.65), so repaired trials are systematically worse than their parents and fail selection.","algorithmic_change":"Before clipping, detect out-of-bounds coordinates; if any exist, resample the offending component(s) uniformly within [lb,ub] instead of clipping, up to K=3 attempts, then fall back to clip. This preserves directional information rather than projecting onto the face.","mathematical_rule":"For each j: if mutant[j] < lb or mutant[j] > ub, then mutant[j] = lb + rand() * (ub - lb); repeat up to K=3 times; if still OOB, mutant[j] = clip(mutant[j], lb, ub).","expected_effect":"Reduces the repair success gap by replacing face-projection with interior resampling, raising repaired-trial success from ~0.12-0.30 toward the 0.33-0.48 no-repair baseline on F1/F7/F10.","failure_prediction":"On high-dimensional or narrow-bound problems (F20), repeated resampling may rarely succeed within K attempts, adding overhead without improving success; fallback clip then dominates.","ablation_plan":"Compare K=1 (clip only), K=2, K=3, and K=5 on F1/F7/F10/F20 across 10 seeds; measure repaired vs non-repaired success rate and OOB rate.","nearest_known_methods":["resampling boundary handling (Brest et al.)","midpoint/reflection repair","uniform random reinitialization of OOB components"],"implementation_requirements":"Modify boundary repair in run_lshade_canonical: add per-component OOB mask, uniform resample loop with K cap, fallback to np.clip; log repair events and success for ablation."}
